top_stories.title: PM Shehbaz departs on 4-day visit to China - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif** departed on a four-day visit to China from May 23 to 26, accompanied by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister **Ishaq Dar**, Planning Minister **Ahsan Iqbal**, Information Minister **Attaullah Tarar**, IT Minister **Shaza Fatima**, and PM’s adviser **Tariq Fatemi**. The visit marks the 75th anniversary of Pakistan-China diplomatic relations and will focus on strengthening bilateral cooperation in political, economic, and strategic domains.  The premier will meet with President Xi Jinping and Premier Li Qiang, discussing topics such as CPEC development, trade, investment, industrial cooperation, agricultural modernization, information technology, science and technology, and people-to-people exchanges.

top_stories.title: Three die in ‘horrific’ south Sydney vehicle crash after police welfare check | Sydney | The Guardian
top_stories.rephrased_article: A **man** died in a crash in Sydney after fleeing from police who had been called to carry out a welfare check. The crash involved a white Audi that rolled over a barrier and struck a blue Toyota sedan, killing the **man**, the driver of the Toyota, and a passenger.  Police believe the Audi was traveling at "considerable speed" when the crash occurred. Investigations are continuing into the circumstances surrounding the incident.

top_stories.title: Centre promised more legislative powers for Ladakh, says delegation - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **The Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)** proposed a new mechanism to grant **Ladakh** greater legislative, financial, and administrative powers within the existing Union Territory framework.  Civil society members who attended a sub-committee meeting with MHA officials on Friday (May 22, 2026) reported that the talks were positive and that the MHA would soon send a draft outlining the proposed changes.

top_stories.title: Seven MLAs from Chennai find place in Tamil Nadu cabinet: highest in recent years - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay** and seven other ministers from Chennai constituencies were sworn in on Thursday, marking a significant representation for the city in the new cabinet.  This is one of the highest contributions to the current cabinet from **Chennai**, with many top leaders from the Tamil Nadu Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) contesting from the city and becoming ministers.

top_stories.title: Kevin Warsh sworn in as Fed chair as Trump faces backlash over economy | Donald Trump | The Guardian
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Kevin Warsh**, hand-picked by **Donald Trump**, was sworn in as chair of the US Federal Reserve, tasked with navigating an uncertain economic outlook.  Warsh faces pressure to cut interest rates despite rising inflation and criticism over his perceived lack of independence from the president.  The new Fed chair pledged a "reform-oriented" approach while acknowledging challenges facing the economy. Public opinion polls show growing dissatisfaction with Trump's economic record, particularly regarding immigration enforcement and affordability issues. The US Federal Reserve faces mounting pressure to address these concerns as Americans grapple with rising fuel prices and inflation.

top_stories.title: Bengali actors face heat after power shift to BJP; FIR filed over 2021 social media posts linked to post-poll violence - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Parambrata Chatterjee**, a Bengali actor, announced he had to align with the **Trinamool Congress** after the recent West Bengal Assembly election results.  He stated this decision was made for his one-year-old son, prompting strong reactions from social media users and fellow actors. **Keya Ghosh**, a BJP leader, responded by criticizing Chatterjee's compromise and highlighting the unwavering support of many BJP supporters in the state.

top_stories.title: The turbulent 15 months of Trump’s unlikely US intelligence director | Trump administration | The Guardian
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Tulsi Gabbard**, the former Democrat and former Hawaii representative, resigned as director of national intelligence on Friday.  Her tenure was marked by tension with **President Donald Trump**, who often excluded her from key conversations and publicly questioned her intelligence assessments. Despite efforts to streamline the agency, Gabbard's relationship with the president deteriorated over time, culminating in a public disagreement about Iran and a perceived partisan approach to her role. Following Gabbard's resignation, **Aaron Lukas** will serve as acting director until June 30th.

top_stories.title: Elected government has no role in Jammu demolitions, says Farooq Abdullah - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Farooq Abdullah**, president of the **National Conference (NC)**, stated that the elected government has no involvement in the ongoing demolitions in Jammu.  He accused the opposition parties of pursuing anti-Gujjar policies and claimed that Gujjars and Bakerwals have historically protected the region's borders. **Gulam Ali Khatana**, a BJP Rajya Sabha member, countered by accusing the NC and Congress of neglecting the development of Gujjar and Pahari communities for decades. He praised the Modi government's efforts to empower these communities.

top_stories.title: Rajasthan Cabinet approves new industrial development policy with focus on talent economy - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: The **Rajasthan** Cabinet approved a new industrial development policy focused on talent economy and private sector participation to create a world-class industrial infrastructure.  **Industries and Commerce Minister Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore** stated the policy would provide incentives for micro, small, and medium enterprises, one district one product, and the export sector. The policy aims to boost the state's economy to $350 billion by 2028-29.  The Cabinet also approved decisions on energy production, water conservation, and pensioners' welfare.

top_stories.title: Tulsi Gabbard resigns as Trump’s top US intelligence official | News | Al Jazeera
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Tulsi Gabbard**, former Democratic congresswoman and presidential candidate, resigned as **Donald Trump**'s director of national intelligence citing her husband's recent diagnosis with a rare form of bone cancer.  She cited her decision to leave the administration in part due to her opposition to US military interventionism, which she has held since serving in the Hawaii National Guard during the Iraq War. The president confirmed Gabbard's resignation and appointed **Aaron Lukas** as acting director.
